prompt.context: In the face of increasing healthcare costs and decreasing margins, our client, the board of trustees for St. Scorekeepers Hospital, is exploring whether a merger would combat market forces. Another local health system also located in Washtenaw County, Mount Ricks Hospital, is a potential target.
prompt.question: Our client would like to evaluate whether a merger would be beneficial to both parties. What are your thoughts?

clarifying_info.q: What departments does each hospital operate?
clarifying_info.a: St. Scorekeepers Hospital has emergency, cardiology, OB/GYN, and orthopedics. Mount Ricks Hospital has emergency, radiology, dermatology, and oncology.

clarifying_info.q: How many patients does each hospital see?
clarifying_info.a: St. Scorekeepers saw 150,000 patients last year; Mount Ricks saw 200,000 patients.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average revenue per patient for each hospital?
clarifying_info.a: St. Scorekeepers averages $150 per patient; Mount Ricks averages $100 per patient.

clarifying_info.q: What are the variable cost rates?
clarifying_info.a: Variable costs are a percentage of average revenue per patient: St. Scorekeepers at 20%, Mount Ricks at 15%.

clarifying_info.q: What are the fixed cost rates?
clarifying_info.a: Fixed costs are a percentage of average revenue per patient: St. Scorekeepers at 40%, Mount Ricks at 30%.
Overhead (legal, IT, HR, finance): St. Scorekeepers = $4.5M, Mount Ricks = $9.75M.
Both hospitals each have 2 facilities; all 4 facilities are in Washtenaw County.

exhibits.title: Historical Revenue per Patient
exhibits.shows: A line chart showing revenue per patient over time (2000–2020) for St. Scorekeepers Hospital, Mount Ricks Hospital, a Regional Competitor, and the National Trend. The y-axis ranges from $50 to $300.

exhibits.title: Hospital Facilities
exhibits.shows: A map of Washtenaw County (red shaded area) showing the geographic locations of St. Scorekeepers Hospital facilities, Mount Ricks Hospital facilities, and a competitor BTB Health System. Legend distinguishes the three systems by symbol.

data.note: Red shaded area represents Washtenaw County

exhibits.title: Service Line Breakdown by Hospital
exhibits.shows: A bar or stacked chart showing the percentage breakdown of service lines (emergency, cardiology, OB/GYN, orthopedics for St. Scorekeepers; emergency, radiology, dermatology, oncology for Mount Ricks) for each hospital. Scale is 0–100%.

framework: Financial Analysis: Calculate current NOI for each hospital (Revenue – Variable Costs – Fixed Costs – Overhead); determine combined NOI baseline
Market Analysis: Review historical revenue trends (Exhibit 1) to understand macro pressure on revenue per patient; assess competitive landscape (BTB Health System)
Customers: Evaluate shifting patient needs, aftercare, digital/telemedicine presence

Potential Synergies: Revenue synergies (wider service range, cross-referral, new distribution channels); Cost synergies (materials/VC reduction via economies of scale, facility/overhead consolidation)
Post-Merger Integration Risks: Cultural clash, new org leadership, regulatory approval, transaction costs, brand equity erosion
Potential Growth Opportunities: Telemedicine, expanded service offerings post-merger

questions.prompt: Calculate the current Net Operating Income (NOI) for St. Scorekeepers Hospital.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build Revenue – VC – FC – Overhead. Strong answer shows clear arithmetic and labels each line.

math.setup: Revenue = patients × avg revenue/patient; VC = patients × (avg rev/patient × VC%); FC = patients × (avg rev/patient × FC%); NOI = Revenue – VC – FC – Overhead

questions.prompt: Calculate the current Net Operating Income (NOI) for Mount Ricks Hospital.
questions.guidance: Same structure as SK. Strong answer notes that despite more patients, lower revenue/patient and high overhead compress NOI.

math.setup: Revenue = patients × avg revenue/patient; VC = patients × (avg rev/patient × VC%); FC = patients × (avg rev/patient × FC%); NOI = Revenue – VC – FC – Overhead
math.answer: Mount Ricks NOI = $1.75M (using overhead of $9.25M per casebook)

questions.prompt: Using the synergy assumptions, calculate NewCo's projected NOI after the merger.
questions.guidance: Candidate applies each synergy factor to the combined baseline, then sums to arrive at NewCo NOI. Strong answer identifies which line items are affected and why.

math.setup: Combined baseline: Revenue $42.5M, VC $7.5M, FC $15.0M, Overhead $13.75M, NOI $6.25M. Apply synergies: Revenue +10%, VC –15%, FC no change, Overhead –30%.
steps: Total cost savings = $1.13M + $0 + $4.13M = $5.25M; revenue uplift = $4.25M; total synergy value = $9.5M
math.answer: NewCo NOI = $15.75M (vs. combined pre-merger NOI of $6.25M); total synergies = $9.5M

questions.prompt: What insights does Exhibit 1 (Historical Revenue per Patient) provide about the merger rationale?
questions.guidance: Average revenue per patient has been declining at both the regional and national level — neither hospital is immune to market forces. This reinforces the need to find structural solutions like a merger to offset revenue pressure.

questions.prompt: What insights does Exhibit 2 (Hospital Facilities map) provide?
questions.guidance: Two of the four facilities are geographically close, suggesting overlapping patient populations. This creates both a risk (cannibalization) and an opportunity (facility consolidation to cut costs). A superior candidate hypothesizes potential to rationalize overlapping facilities.

questions.prompt: What insights does Exhibit 3 (Service Line Breakdown) provide?
questions.guidance: The only overlapping service line between St. Scorekeepers and Mount Ricks is the Emergency department. All other service lines are complementary. This means the merged entity can offer a significantly wider range of services, enabling cross-referral and retaining more patients within the system — supporting the 10% revenue synergy assumption.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the variable and fixed costs a hospital typically faces?

recommendation: Recommend the merger between St. Scorekeepers Hospital and Mount Ricks Hospital. The combined NewCo would generate $15.75M in net operating income — compared to a combined pre-merger NOI of $6.25M — representing $9.5M in synergy value from revenue growth and cost consolidation.
risks: Regulatory roadblocks: merger may not receive antitrust or healthcare regulatory approval
Logistical complexity of completing a multi-facility, multi-department merger
Erosion of brand equity for either or both hospital brands
Cultural clash between employees and clinicians of the two health systems
Analysis does not include transaction costs, which could reduce net benefit
next_steps: Announce merger and prepare for regulatory review process
Reach out to insurance companies (payors) to negotiate improved reimbursement rates, leveraging increased scale
Develop unified branding and patient communication strategy to inform patients of the new, enhanced healthcare system
